messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: rediscloud-auth upstream errors > 60s, cache client 5xx/403 spike observed (service: managed-cache, region: eu-west-1)
incidents-bot: Alert level: P1 · affected routes: token-lookup, rate-limiter, prefix-cache
anna (SRE): oncall here, seeing repeated `ERR auth failed` from redis client libs, many callers falling through to origin -> rate limiter is tripping due to cache misses
matt (Oncall): ack, I'm pulling logs. are we seeing auth token TTL or handshake errors?
anna (SRE): looks like `ERR invalid password` from rediscloud side. grep: `2026-11-05T09:12:03Z client=svc-auth pid=... ERR invalid password` across multiple clusters
jamie (Eng): rolling deploy of token rotation last night? any change in our side?
taylor (Platform): no deploys touching cache credentials. last rotation was automated by rediscloud yesterday (they said rotating keys for some tenants).
lee (Support): customers hitting 502s on endpoints that rely on cached rate-limiter keys. Support queue has ~12 tickets mentioning 502/timeout for inference requests in EU.
anna (SRE): immediate mitigation plan: 1) switch reads that tolerate stale data to local memcached fallback 2) temporarily disable strict auth validation in rate-limiter path (read-only) 3) raise rate-limiter soft limit to avoid aggressive global throttles
matt (Oncall): doing 1) now — enabling memcached fallback in feature flag `cache-fallback:enabled` for eu services. Command: ``kubectl set env deployment/rl-service CACHE_FALLBACK=memcached-eu -n prod``
jamie (Eng): I'm patching rate-limiter to skip token-validation on failures (safe mode) and returning conservative allow instead of hard-block. pushing canary to 2 pods
anna (SRE): added temporary firewall rule to prefer memcached endpoints to reduce pressure on rediscloud until they confirm fix.
incidents-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started for rl-service canary (2/12 pods) by jamie at 09:20Z
matt (Oncall): noticed latencies drop after fallback, error rate for 502s decreased from 7% -> 1.8% within 6m. firming metrics: `rate-limiter.errors` down, `origin.latency` still elevated for some scorable flows
alice (Security): any risk from skipping auth validation? we need to ensure no privilege escalation — this is read-only fallback, only cached rate tokens.
jamie (Eng): verified logic: fallback does not allow escalation; token->scope mapping still enforced client-side. added extra logs to monitor for anomalous permissions
lee (Support): drafting proactive customer message: "We're experiencing degraded caching in EU due to downstream Redis provider auth rotation. We've enabled fallbacks to reduce impact — some requests may still see higher latency. Engineers are on call." Want approval to send to top 50 affected orgs
matt (Oncall): approve. include ETA: initial mitigation in place, awaiting rediscloud confirmation.
anna (SRE): reached out to RedisCloud via partner Slack and support case [RC-#98764], they acknowledged and are investigating key rotation job that may have left old tokens active but rejected by edge nodes. Asking for emergency rollback or key re-issue
incidents-bot: Note: oncall handoff scheduled at 09:30Z — matt -> taylor as primary after handoff
matt (Oncall): handing off to taylor at 09:30Z, summary: fallback enabled, soft-limits increased, customer comms drafted, awaiting upstream fix.
taylor (Platform): taking over. I'll keep tracking RedisCloud case and validate metrics. re-running healthcheck across eu clusters (command: `scripts/healthcheck --env=prod --region=eu-west-1`)
anna (SRE): observed intermittent 403s still but much reduced. cache miss rate stabilized at ~4% (was 28%).
jamie (Eng): added an automated revert to strict-auth after 1h if RedisCloud confirms fix; manual patch to remove after postmortem
incidents-bot: RedisCloud update at 09:44Z: We rolled back last-night rotation for affected tenants, should be stable within 10 minutes for connections that re-auth
matt (Oncall): seeing reconnects succeed; error graph trending to baseline.
lee (Support): sending updated customer note: "Redis provider rotated keys; we enabled fallbacks and requests are recovering. We will follow up with a root cause and mitigation steps." Sent to affected orgs at 09:50Z
alice (Security): recommend follow-up audit on credentials rotation handling and tighter circuit-breakers for third-party auth failures
taylor (Platform): agreed. postmortem task list: 1) add better grace for key-rotation (cached creds TTL + jitter) 2) automated memcached fallback test 3) stricter alerting for auth-failure spikes 4) vendor SLAs + runbook for key rotations
anna (SRE): marking incident as degraded -> mitigated at 09:54Z. full resolution pending vendor RCA.
incidents-bot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 09:54Z (metrics returning to normal but follow-up required)
matt (Oncall): final note — lessons: vendor rotations need scheduled cross-team notice, ensure token refresh logic tolerates transient rejections. I'll own the follow-up with RedisCloud and schedule postmortem 24h window
lee (Support): will attach support ticket list and customer impact summary to the postmortem doc
taylor (Platform): logging final state and linking to postmortem: https://redwood-internal/postmortems/1824567890-rediscloud-rotation-fallback — assign owners for each action item
anna (SRE): thanks all. closing thread once postmortem is filed.
